spec.title: PROP-076 — The cache-stable SYSTEM prompt prefix
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-07; design settled 2026-11-10 against the tree at `e2508fc1d`. Status `spec/plan`: nothing is implemented. The owner's shape is the research proposal `campaigns/next-semantic-transfer-2026-11/architecture/SYSTEM-PROMPT-SPEC.md` and its machine form `system-prompt.json`; the decisions below settle every choice that document left open, against the actual code rather than against the 2026-11-07 survey, which carried seven wrong file paths and three wrong behavioural claims (`#SYS-BASELINE-CORRECTIONS`). Implementation follows the corporate-environment and application-version campaigns (campaign node `SYS-PROMPT`, after `APP-VERSIONS`); the plan is `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/PLAN.md`. This document is a design, not an acceptance: no fact below is evidence that any part of the feature exists.

p.SYS-PURPOSE: A project can hand an API caller one byte-stable block of instructions instead of asking an agent to re-read its boot lane. The user writes `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` — ordinary permanent instructions, no language, no directives — and `vibe` generates `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/SYSTEM.md`: the user's frame, the selected repository entrypoint, and the already-compiled static boot lane, in one deterministic UTF-8 text fit for the instruction role of an API request. The same relevant inputs always give the same bytes, so a provider that caches on an exact prefix match can cache it; a change of task never changes it; and a stale copy is detected before a request is sent rather than silently believed. The live part of boot — the current INDEX inputs and the session's own context — follows that prefix at request time and is never frozen into it. What this buys is the *conditions* for a cache hit and an honest freshness claim, never a promised hit, TTL or percentage saved.

p.SYS-SIZE-TODAY: The scale, measured on this repository at `e2508fc1d` and re-measured at `c04bda8a5`, is why the feature exists: the compiled lane `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/STATIC.xml` is 251,817 bytes, the entrypoint `AGENTS.md` is 26,121 bytes, and the eight files `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/INDEX.md` names are 57,894 bytes together — 335,832 bytes of boot material, of which **75% is the one compiled lane** (251,817 / 335,832 = 74.98%) and **83% (the lane plus the entrypoint) changes only when packages, authored boot sources or the template change** (277,938 / 335,832 = 82.76%). That 83% is the prefix this document specifies; assembled it measures 278,092 bytes, or 82.81% of the boot material (spike S1, 2026-11-10). The remaining 17% is the continuation, which is byte-stable too but stays late-bound on purpose (`#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX`). **Amended 2026-11-10 by spike S1:** this fact read **92% / 8%** when written, which was an arithmetic slip — `(251,817 + 26,121) / 335,832` is 82.76%, not 92%. The slip had been copied into `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/PLAN.md` §5, `FORMAT-CHANGES.md` `SP-FMT-003` and the campaign log, and all four are corrected. Nothing in the design depended on the number; it is a release-note figure.

boundary.title: 2. The prefix and the live continuation

p.SYS-BANDS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — four bands, and exactly one of them is a generated file.** **Band P, the prefix**: the bytes of `SYSTEM.md`, in three segments — the literal template, the entrypoint export, and the compiled static lane. **Band U, the unconditional continuation**: the admitted bytes of every INDEX entry with no residual `when`, in INDEX order. **Band G, the gated continuation**: every INDEX entry carrying a residual `when`, each evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target. **Band T, the task**: the session context, the conversation and the request. Band P is a committed artifact; bands U and G are a *plan* in `SYSTEM.meta.json` that a runner executes at request time by reading the current files; band T is the caller's own and never appears in any witness. The pair (P, U+G) covers the whole **computable** boot of the selected node; band T is everything else. The four-band split is the whole design: it is what lets the big stable text be a file while the late-bound text stays late-bound.

p.SYS-BAND-ORDER: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the order inside band P, and why the boot law and the cache agree.** The three segments are, in order: **(1)** the template, **(2)** the entrypoint export, **(3)** the static lane. That is PROP-009 `#SESSION-START-ORDER` with the user's own frame prepended — redirect, then `STATIC`, then (in bands U and G) the INDEX entries — so no authored instruction is reordered relative to any other. It is *also* the cache-optimal order, which is the design's one piece of luck and is recorded so nobody "optimises" it later: a provider cache matches a **prefix**, so an edit to an early segment invalidates every later one. The lane is the segment that changes most often (every `vibe install` that moves the resolution can move it) and the template is the segment that changes least often (a human edits it deliberately, rarely), so putting the lane **last** means a lane change costs only the lane's own cache entry, while the reverse order would make every lane change invalidate the template and the entrypoint too. The two constraints point the same way; neither is being traded against the other.

p.SYS-NOT-COMPLETE-BOOT: **`SYSTEM.md` alone is not a session.** The prefix is not declared a snapshot of everything a session needs, and a caller that sends it alone gets an explicitly incomplete boot. Obligations an authored entrypoint states beyond reading files — resolve a user-local context, read a plan, consult a campaign document — are not discharged by generation and are not reported as discharged: an agent with tools performs them, or the calling program supplies the material through its own runtime contract. An exporter never claims to have read what it did not read. This is the honest boundary, stated once, so that no later convenience ("ship the one file") can be mistaken for a complete contract.

p.SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `kind = "static"` in INDEX is not permission to compile.** An INDEX row's `kind` describes *read timing*, not linkage: PROP-009 `#AUTHORED-INDEX-BOUNDARY` says so in words and `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts.rs:203-207` says so in code, where the kind is literally `if e.when.is_some() { "dynamic" } else { "static" }` over entries that `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot.rs:314`/`:336` have already forced to `LinkType::Dynamic` + `PackageFormat::Simple`. PROP-072 `#SOURCE-HOST-BOOT-LAW` repeats the rule from the source side. Therefore no INDEX entry's bytes enter `SYSTEM.md`, however unconditional the row, and a second "freeze the whole INDEX" profile is **not** offered in this version: it would contradict dynamic linking, make freshness far harder to prove, and buy nothing that `#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE` does not already buy. A target-bound full snapshot remains a separate contract for a separate request, named in `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q1.

p.SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — band U is cacheable without being frozen, and that is the whole reason the boundary costs nothing.** Band U's bytes are the current bytes of files whose *identity and order* the boot plan fixes; they change only when those files change, exactly as band P's do. A provider that supports several cache breakpoints can therefore place one at the end of band P and another at the end of band U, and a task change still invalidates neither. `prepare` makes this possible by returning bands P, U, G and the recommended breakpoint positions **as separate, ordered materials with their own observed digests**, not as one concatenated string. So the design gives up nothing by keeping INDEX late-bound: the bytes are cached either way, and the one thing not given up is the runtime meaning of a dynamic entry. The only residual cost against a frozen artifact is that a runner must read band U's files per request, which is local file reading of 57,894 bytes on this repository.

p.SYS-FILES: **Decided 2026-11-10 — three paths, three roles, under the selected node's `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/`.** `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` is **authored** by the user: literal permanent text, the only input the user writes, never rewritten by `vibe`. `SYSTEM.md` is **generated**: the prefix bytes of `#SYS-BANDS`. `SYSTEM.meta.json` is **generated**: the versioned sidecar of `#SYS-SIDECAR` — the input witnesses, the segment map and the continuation plan. **Amended 2026-11-10 by the owner decision `#SYS-ARTIFACTS-NOT-TRACKED`, which supersedes `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q6:** neither generated file is git-tracked. This fact read "git-tracked and marked generated like `STATIC`/`INDEX` (PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-GENERATED`), so a fresh clone boots by pure file reading and never by running a build"; that reasoning belongs to the boot lane, which a session reads, and not to a prefix, which only a program that is already running `vibe` ever consumes. A third generated file joins them under the same rule: the agent lane of `#SYS-AGENT-LANE`. Editing `SYSTEM.md` by hand is not a supported way to configure anything; the supported way is the template and `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE`. The `.md` extension of `SYSTEM.md` is a name, not a parse: nothing reads the file as Markdown, and its lane segment holds XML bytes verbatim (`#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`).

p.SYS-ARTIFACTS-NOT-TRACKED: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — the generated prefix, its sidecar and the agent lane are not git-tracked, and `vibe` writes the `.gitignore` that says so. This supersedes `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q6.** The three generated files are produced by `vibe install` for a node that has opted in, and by `vibe prompt build`; `vibe prompt prepare` rebuilds a stale one or refuses, never sends it. They are covered by a `.gitignore` **vibe itself writes into the boot directory it owns** — the repository root `.gitignore` is never touched, because that file is the developer's. One rule now covers every prefix in the system: PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION` already forbids committing the composed prefix, and a project layer that was tracked while the composite was not would have been two rules for one kind of artifact. **Why, in the owner's terms.** The prefix is fully derivable from committed inputs — the template, the entrypoint, the compiled lane and `[system_prompt]` — and its generation is deterministic (`#SYS-DETERMINISM`), so the artifact carries no fact its inputs do not. Committing it would duplicate roughly 280 KB of text that is already in the repository twice over, invite a merge conflict in a file no human can usefully merge, and let a stale copy be committed and then believed. **`vibe check` reports it as an error when git tracks a generated prefix**, naming the path and the remedy, because a tracked copy is the one state the rule exists to prevent. The boot lane keeps the opposite rule for the opposite reason: `STATIC.*` and `INDEX.md` are read by a session with no tools but a file reader, so they must survive a fresh clone (PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-GENERATED`). A prefix is read by a program that is already running `vibe`. Format record: `SP-FMT-102`.

p.SYS-AGENT-LANE: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — there are two generated prompt artifacts, not one, and the second one is the lane alone.** `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/AGENT-LANE.md` is the **agent-mode** artifact: `STATIC.*` followed by every unconditional INDEX file in INDEX order, each wrapped in the marker pair of `#SYS-LANE-MARKERS`. It carries **no template, no entrypoint, no router block and no import line**. It is therefore not `SYSTEM.md` minus a segment: `SYSTEM.md` is band P (template + entrypoint + lane) for an API caller, while the agent lane is the lane part of band P plus the whole of band U, for a harness's own instruction slot. `vibe agent` **recomposes it at every launch** from the files then on disk, which is how band U keeps the "current bytes" meaning `#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX` gives it; it is generated and never tracked (`#SYS-ARTIFACTS-NOT-TRACKED`). Under a fixed `host` the matching `os:` rows are baked in as further marked segments; under `"portable"` they are not in the file at all and the router has the agent read them (`#SYS-HARNESS-DELIVERY`). Design document: `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` §1.1. Format record: `SP-FMT-103`.

p.SYS-OPT-IN: **Decided 2026-11-10 — presence of the template is the opt-in, and nothing else is.** No template, no generation and no change whatever to the node's boot: `vibe install` behaves byte-for-byte as it does today, which is what makes this feature free for every project that does not want it. A present but empty template means "opt in with no frame of my own" and generates a prefix of the entrypoint export plus the lane. `vibe init` may **offer** to create a template; no installation ever creates, overwrites or deletes an authored template. Opting out is deleting the template, which removes only the two provably-owned generated outputs (`#SYS-REMOVAL-AND-CONFLICT`).

p.SYS-TEMPLATE-LITERAL: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the template is text, not a program, and this version introduces no template language at all.** There is no shell, no environment or `HOME` read, no `INCLUDE`, no network, no conditionals, no slot grammar and no placement directives. Curly braces, fenced examples, Markdown links and the literal strings `SYSTEM.md` or `<vibevm>` inside the template are ordinary characters with no effect — which is the point of `#SYS-SELF-INCLUSION`'s rule that self-reference is judged over semantic edges, never over prose. `vibe` appends the two contract-defined segments after the template's bytes; where they go is fixed by `#SYS-BAND-ORDER` and is not the author's choice. Controlled placement (a declared insertion point) is a later, separate extension, and deliberately not this version's problem: the useful feature does not need it, and a grammar is the one thing that cannot be taken back.

p.SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the tuning that is not text goes in the manifest, following PROP-075 `#TEMPLATE-SPELLING` exactly. Implemented 2026-11-10.** One new optional top-level table `[system_prompt]` on the node's own `vibe.toml`, with exactly three optional members in this version: `entrypoint` (default `"AGENTS.md"`, admitted only from the closed set `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` — the same set `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:29` already owns — or the boolean `false` meaning "no entrypoint segment"), `lane_form` (`"verbatim"`, the default and in this version the only accepted value, reserved so `#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`'s alternative needs no format change), and `recipe` (an integer pinning the generated-text recipe of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT`; absent means the current one). The typed section is `SystemPromptSection { entrypoint: EntrypointChoice, lane_form: LaneForm, recipe: Option<u32> }` with `EntrypointChoice::{Default, File(EntrypointFile), None}` and `LaneForm::Verbatim`; the closed set is spelled `EntrypointFile` and **not** `RedirectFile`, because `vibe_core::manifest::RedirectFile` is already the unrelated `vibe-redirect.toml` document, and a test in vibe-workspace pins `EntrypointFile::ALL` to `REDIRECT_FILES` so the two crates' spellings cannot drift. A bad value fails **deserialisation** rather than defaulting, the pattern `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package/when.rs` already establishes: `lane_form = "projected"` refuses as reserved instead of silently behaving as verbatim, an `entrypoint` outside the closed set refuses while naming all three legal spellings, and `entrypoint = true` refuses because it says nothing. `[system_prompt]` present with no `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` beside it is a validation refusal naming the TOML path, by the rule of PROP-059 `#declaration` that every refusal names its field as a TOML path; because that refusal needs a directory it is `Manifest::validate_system_prompt_beside`, called from `Manifest::read`, and a manifest parsed from a string is deliberately not checked. The table is added to `Manifest`, to `ManifestWire` (`deny_unknown_fields`) and to both `TryFrom` arms, so an unknown member is refused by name. The table is legal on **every** role, including a bare `[project]`: the prefix is a property of the selected node, so it is not a package-role section and does not join the "package-role section without `[package]`" refusal. Every member is omitted when absent, so every existing manifest serialises byte-identically. Nothing else is configurable in this version — no inclusion policy, no segment order, no OS baking.

p.SYS-LAYOUT-RESERVATION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the three paths join the one shared layout owner, each in its own role, and the research's "do not label the template generated" warning is honoured literally. Implemented 2026-11-10 exactly as designed.** `crates/vibe-core/src/layout.rs` gains `SYSTEM_MD`, `SYSTEM_META_JSON` and `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE_MD` beside `INDEX_MD`, `STATIC_XML` and `STATIC_MD`, with `current_boot_system()`, `current_boot_system_meta()` and `current_boot_system_template()` beside `current_boot_index()`. The private `generated_boot_paths()` gains the two **generated** paths and so returns five, and a new private `reserved_boot_paths()` adds the authored template to make the six paths declaration admission refuses; `is_generated_boot_output` and `is_reserved_boot_source` keep their existing exact-match and ASCII-case-alias semantics, and every existing caller inherited the exclusion at once with no call-site edit — the prediction `PLAN.md` §5 made about the twelve callers held. The **authored** template gets a *separate* predicate `is_reserved_boot_authored_input`, not membership in `generated_boot_paths`: it is excluded from automatic boot enrolment and from declaration admission as a source row, but it is not generated, is not owned by publication, is never deleted as a stale output, and is preserved like any authored file. Collapsing the two roles into one list would be the convenient mistake that loses the template on a format change, so the three-way classification — each path in exactly one role, all three in the one boot directory, pairwise distinct — is pinned by its own unit test.

p.SYS-SELF-INCLUSION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact hazard, the exact three gates, and the exact test for self-reference. Gates (a), (b) and (c) are implemented; the generator-side input-list refusal waits for the generator.** The hazard was real at `c04bda8a5` and not hypothetical: `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/own_boot.rs:167` `legacy_entries` enumerates the immediate children of the boot directory and admits every one that `vibe_specdoc::is_spec_source` accepts — which is, by extension alone, every `.md` and `.xml` file (`crates/vibe-specdoc/src/load.rs:76-81`) — excluding only `STATIC.md`, `STATIC.xml` and `INDEX.md` by name (`:185-190`). **Spike S3 demonstrated it and corrected its shape.** Dropped in unprepared, both `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` were indeed admitted as ordinary boot inputs — a fixture boot directory holding two authored snippets plus the two new names produced **four** `INDEX.md` rows, each `kind = "static"`, so every session would read the generated prefix a second time and the template's text would arrive twice. **The predicted *recursive growth* did not reproduce, and this fact overstated it:** a node's own authored boot is forced to `LinkType::Dynamic` unconditionally (`crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot.rs:314`/`:336`), so its bytes never enter the compiled lane — the files are only *named* in INDEX. Two consecutive regenerations left the lane empty and `INDEX.md` byte-identical at 883 bytes. The hazard is therefore **doubled delivery, silently**, not a growing artifact: a literal template in no spec dialect was admitted without any error, because an INDEX row is never parsed at generation time. That is the quieter and more dangerous version of the same bug, and it is what the gates close. The three gates that must all learn the names are **(a)** the legacy immediate-children scan above, now asking the layout owner's two predicates instead of comparing three bare names, **(b)** the automatic native discovery in `crates/vibe-spec/src/source_policy/authored_boot.rs:74-129`, which already skips generated outputs at `:97` through `is_generated_boot_output` and so inherits the two generated paths for free, needing an explicit arm only for the authored template, and **(c)** declaration admission, `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/source_descriptor/mod.rs:228`, which already refuses reserved boot paths including ASCII case aliases. **The test for self-reference is an admitted semantic edge or a file identity, never a string.** A template that discusses `SYSTEM.md`, links to it in Markdown, or shows it in a fenced example is ordinary literal text and is admitted; a declared source row, a boot snippet binding or a path alias that actually resolves to one of the three paths is refused **before** anything is written, naming the path and the edge. An output listed in its own inputs, directly or through any alias the layout owner recognises, is the same refusal — that last clause binds the generator and is not yet implemented, because no generator exists.

p.SYS-ENTRYPOINT-ONE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — exactly one entrypoint, of the selected node, never a filesystem walk.** The default is the selected node's own `AGENTS.md`; `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE` may name `CLAUDE.md` or `GEMINI.md` instead, or `false` for none. The three are never concatenated: by this repository's own convention they are kept byte-identical, so joining them triples the text, and in a project where they differ by harness, joining them delivers contradictions. Ancestor or external instruction files are not discovered by walking the filesystem: inheritance is whatever the selected-node effective-boot contract already computes (PROP-009 `#FOUNDATION-DOWN`, `#MATRYOSHKA-SCOPES`), and an explicitly added harness input appears in the sidecar's input list like any other. A node with no entrypoint file and no `false` declaration is a refusal naming the expected path, not a silent empty segment.

p.SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the managed block is replaced in place, at its own byte range, and nothing else in the document is touched.** The entrypoint carries a vibe-owned `<vibevm>` managed block (PROP-009 `#REDIRECT-MANAGED-BLOCK`, PROP-012) whose whole content is boot instructions. `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:128` `locate_block` already returns that block's exact `start`/`end` byte offsets, refuses a malformed or mismatched marker pair rather than repairing it, and matches only an exactly standalone `<vibevm>` / `</vibevm>` line. The export takes the entrypoint's admitted bytes, and substitutes the transport contract of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT` for exactly the bytes between those offsets. Three consequences, each deliberate: the generated text sits in the one position where generated text already sits today, so no authored paragraph moves; the authored preamble that also orders a full boot is answered at the same relative distance it is answered today; and a malformed marker pair is a named refusal, never a regex repair of a co-tenant document. A node whose entrypoint has no managed block at all is admitted with its bytes whole and the contract appended as its own trailing segment — stated here so the common case and the no-block case do not need two readings of the same rule.

p.SYS-NO-REWRITE-OF-AUTHORED-TEXT: **The exporter never summarises, shortens, reorders or filters authored instructions.** No model touches the text; no heuristic decides a paragraph is "not suitable for an API"; no absolute path an author wrote is edited away. The one structurally-owned region named in `#SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE` is the only substitution. The generator's own restriction against volatile content (`#SYS-NO-VOLATILE`) binds the generator, not the author: an authored absolute path, machine fact or operating-facts ledger entry passes through verbatim, and the most diagnostics may do is *report* that such content makes the prefix less portable or more volatile. It never changes policy silently, and a warning is not a licence to edit.

p.SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — what the one piece of generated prose says, and what it carefully does not say.** The contract is a short, versioned, generated block (`recipe`, `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE`) that states, as plain facts about this request: which sources have been supplied in it, each by role and relative path; that their content is already present and need not be read again **to discharge those same boot obligations**; that the continuation entries actually supplied are named where they appear; and that any entry not named has **not** been supplied and must not be treated as read. It is the honest answer to the problem that some authored paragraphs legitimately order a `STATIC` read: rather than guessing which sentences those are and editing them, the transport states what transport did. Four things it must not do. It does not forbid tool calls in general — a later instruction to check the current state of a file on disk remains perfectly valid, and no text can guarantee an agent makes no tool call anyway; that is a property of the adapter and of agent behaviour, proved by `#SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT`'s tests, not asserted by prose. It does not instruct the agent to run `vibe` or anything else: PROP-009 `#PURE-FILE-READING` and `#REJ-RUN-VIBE` forbid turning boot into a command, and `prepare` is the *calling program's* preflight, never the model's errand (`#SYS-READ-ONLY-CHECK`). It carries no digest, build time, path or counter, so it cannot be the thing that makes two otherwise equal prefixes differ. And it speaks only for its own layer, which is what lets `#SYS-LAYER-CONCATENATION` add more layers later without rewriting it.

p.SYS-ENTRYPOINT-IS-AN-INPUT: **The entrypoint is a build input, so a prefix can change with no package change at all.** Editing the entrypoint's authored prose — a new convention, a corrected rule, a line in an operating-facts ledger — changes the prefix, and the generator does not hide that to protect a cache. The claim this design makes is "the same relevant inputs give the same bytes", never "unchanged until the package list changes". The honest consequence is that a repository whose entrypoint carries frequently-edited current-state material pays a cache write per edit; the remedy is to move that material out of the entrypoint, which is a repository-hygiene decision for its owner and not something the exporter may take on their behalf.

p.SYS-LANE-VERBATIM: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the lane enters as the admitted bytes, opaque, and is not re-parsed, re-compiled or projected.** `vibe` has a read-only in-memory analyser that shares composer, table, hoist, de-substitution, source bindings and freshness admission with the write path (`crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/analyze.rs`, whose provider-free `analyze_node_lane` at `:80` ends in an in-memory compile at `:216`), and **three** independent lane prepare-and-compile sites, each with its own `entries.is_empty() → None` gate — the builtin seam `boot_artifacts/compile.rs:86` `compile_static_artifact_with_plans` (`:100-103`), the owner-managed seam `boot_artifacts/native_managed.rs:232` (`:260-263`), and the custom-backend seam `boot_artifacts/native_managed/explicit.rs:22` (`:35-38`). **Refined 2026-11-10 by spike S4 — only two of the three publish a node's STATIC lane, and they are mutually exclusive per run.** The seam is chosen once for a whole regeneration, not per node: `install/bootgen.rs:242` drives every node through the builtin loop, while `install/bootgen.rs:262` `regenerate_boot_from_traced_native_prepared` drives every node through `install/bootgen/native_managed.rs:39` instead, so within one run no node mixes them. Instrumented, the real host node reached the builtin seam only (26 static inputs, artifact 251,817 bytes, byte-equal to the committed lane); across vibe-workspace's whole lib suite the builtin seam fired 206 times and the owner-managed seam 208, in disjoint tests. The custom-backend seam is **not** a STATIC-lane producer at all: it compiles `artifacts/<backend>` and is reached only through the `compile_node_backend*` analyser queries (`install/bootgen/analyze.rs:415`, exported from `install.rs:98`), never from a boot publication path — it fired exactly once in the whole suite. The prefix therefore reuses that output as **one admitted segment** through whichever of the **two publishing** seams the node's own world selected — it does not add a third publishing seam, and it does not assume one; it never re-enters the compiler as a fresh normal source, which would risk doubled qualification, lost attribution and duplicate expansion, and it never follows a `#use` marker, a provenance comment or a `spec://` reference found in the text. Three mechanisms in the lane keep their meaning untouched because nothing reads inside the segment: normal-closure source-identity coverage (PROP-009 `#NORMAL-CLOSURE-ONCE`), compiled-unit de-substitution with its deliberate partial-coverage residual (`#STATIC-EMITS-ONCE-EACH`), and soft hoisting's `#use` markers. The alternative — an explicitly selected canonical Markdown projection through PROP-072 `#SOURCE-GENERATED-XML-PROJECTION-LAW` — is **rejected for this version** and reserved as `lane_form = "projected"`: it would make a prompt build fail on an unrepresentable placement, and it changes the token stream, which would confound the one differential proof this campaign has (that the prefix delivers what a file-reading agent reads). Original generated bytes and any future projected bytes are different facts with different digests, and the sidecar would name which it holds.

p.SYS-LANE-SPELLING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the lane's spelling and absence are the existing owner's answers, not the exporter's.** Which of `STATIC.md` / `STATIC.xml` exists is decided by `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/format.rs:42` `resolve_static_path`, which returns the one present path, `None` when neither is present, and a **refusal** when both are (`:50-55`, "the generator owns one; delete the stray"). The exporter retains all three answers exactly: it records the selected spelling in the sidecar, it builds a valid prefix with **no** lane segment when a node has no static contributions, and it propagates the both-present refusal rather than picking a side. A first generation on a node that has never had a lane is therefore a normal case, not an error, and the analyser's dialect fallback for an uncommitted spelling is reported rather than silently resolved.

p.SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact framing, because determinism lives in these details.** Each segment is introduced by a single frame line of a fixed generated form carrying the layer-qualified segment id and nothing variable — no digest, no length, no time, no path of the checkout. The frame token is distinct from the lane's own `vibe:c1` comments and is never an exactly standalone `<vibevm>` or `</vibevm>` line, so `locate_block` can never mistake a frame for a managed marker and a frame can never be mistaken for lane content. **Frames use LF and the file ends with exactly one LF**; a segment **body** is the admitted bytes verbatim, with one LF inserted before the next frame when the body does not already end with one, so an authored CRLF document keeps its own line endings inside its own segment and the surrounding structure is identical on every host. The repository-wide `* text=auto eol=lf` of `.gitattributes:7` is what makes that identity survive a Windows checkout, and the determinism claim of `#SYS-DETERMINISM` depends on it — a project without that attribute gets a prefix that differs by checkout, which diagnostics report. Text separators are structure for a reader, never a security boundary: `#SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT` says the same thing about roles.

p.SYS-LANE-MARKERS: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — every lane segment is wrapped in a deterministic begin/end pair, and the reliable half of what they buy is offline.** Each segment of the agent lane is framed by `<!-- vibe:lane-begin <node-id> <path> <hash12> -->` and the matching `vibe:lane-end` line, where `<path>` is the file's project-relative path (not a label — the truncation rule must tell the model *which file* to read, and the path is that answer), `<hash12>` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the segment bytes between the two lines, and `<node-id>` is the selected node's identity, without which a nested project's block could match an outer project's lane. The lines carry no `@`, are ordinary HTML/XML comments, and are a pure function of the inputs, so they cost nothing in cache stability; `STATIC.xml` already opens with `<!-- vibe:c1 … -->` lines, so the convention is not new. **Markers exist only in the composed lane; the files on disk are untouched** — `vibe` does not own `90-user.xml`. **Four uses, and exactly one of them is a mechanism.** Presence (both lines present ⇒ do not read that file), truncation (a begin with no end ⇒ read it from disk), duplication (the same pair twice ⇒ follow one copy), and staleness (the delivered `STATIC` hash differs from the expected one the managed block states ⇒ read the lane from disk). All four are *instructions to a model* in the session, and a model can skip a comparison or miss a missing end marker in 300 KB of text. What can be relied on is `vibe prompt check`, offline: every begin has its end, pairs are unique, order matches INDEX, each hash matches its own bytes, the block's expected hash matches the current `STATIC.*`, and no marker-shaped line occurs inside a segment's own bytes. Only `STATIC.*` gets an expected hash in the managed block; a live INDEX file gets markers and no expected value, so editing `90-user.xml` never rewrites `AGENTS.md`. The stated cost of that one hash is that all three entrypoint copies change whenever the lane changes — accepted deliberately — and it never enters `SYSTEM.md`, because composition replaces the managed block (`#SYS-NO-RECURSION`). Design document: `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` §2. Format record: `SP-FMT-104`.

identity.title: 6. Identity, freshness and determinism

p.SYS-TWO-IDENTITIES: **Two different facts, never conflated.** `prefix_sha256` is the digest of the bytes actually in `SYSTEM.md` — it proves byte identity and nothing else. The **input witness** is the ordered list of the observed inputs the text was built from, together with the selected node, entrypoint, recipe, lane spelling and boot-plan identity — it proves *consistency* between an output and a set of observations. Neither proves authenticity: the existing boot-graph verifier is graph verification and explicitly not body authentication (PROP-072 `#SOURCE-BOOT-CHECK-LAW`), and the existing unit fingerprint (`crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs:133` `compute`) hashes identity, own path, resolved version, conditions, fragments, edge modes, child fingerprints, optional owner-plan digests and native-pending frames and performs **no file read at all** — so it cannot stand in for an input witness, and the node lane carries no fingerprint anyway (`boot_artifacts.rs:379`, `:394-395`). A matching digest with a matching witness means "this text is what these observations produce"; it never means "these observations are trustworthy" or "this prefix is what a provider cached".

p.SYS-SIDECAR: **Decided 2026-11-10 — what version 1 of the sidecar holds, and the four things it must not hold.** `SYSTEM.meta.json`, protocol `vibe-system-prompt/1`, described by a new JTD schema and a new format-registry record (`#SYS-FORMAT-CHANGES`): the protocol tag; the **relative** identity of the selected node; the entrypoint's relative path or `false`; the recipe version; the lane spelling (`static-md` / `static-xml` / `none`) and `lane_form`; the `layer` role (`#SYS-LAYER-ROLE`); an ordered `inputs[]` of the prefix's inputs, each with its role, its path relative to the node, the SHA-256 of the bytes **as observed** and their length; `prefix_sha256` and `prefix_len`; a `segments[]` map of id, byte offset, length and whether the segment is recommended as a cache boundary; the boot-plan identity the existing owner produces, together with the SHA-256 of `INDEX.md`'s bytes; and the `continuation` plan — the ordered rows of bands U and G, each with its path relative to the node, its band, and for a gated row its `when` string verbatim. **It must not hold**: a build time or any timestamp; an absolute checkout, `HOME` or cache path; the generating host's operating system or any environment observation; and **no content digest for any continuation row** — the reason is `#SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME`. A sidecar is therefore a pure function of the prefix inputs and the boot plan, which is what makes a second `vibe install` with nothing changed produce byte-identical files and no git diff.

p.SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the continuation's bytes are witnessed per request, never in the committed artifact, and this is the decision that keeps dynamic linking meaningful.** Putting a hash of `90-user.xml` in the sidecar would make every edit of a user boot snippet dirty a committed generated file and demand a regeneration — destroying the one property dynamic linking exists for, that an authored snippet's bytes may change and be read fresh without a rebuild. So the committed witness covers the prefix inputs and the *plan* (its order, its paths, its conditions, the digest of the `INDEX.md` bytes that fix them), and `prepare` reports the continuation's observed digests in its **response**, as request-local observations. The practical rule follows directly and is the one in `#SYS-INVALIDATION`: changed dynamic bytes under an unchanged plan give a new suffix and leave the prefix valid; a changed plan — a new, removed or reordered entry, a changed condition, changed visibility, a different selected node or a different package binding — invalidates the pairing and must be recomputed under the current world rather than paired blindly with an old prefix.

p.SYS-NO-VOLATILE: **The generator inserts nothing volatile into the stable bytes.** No build time, no absolute checkout or `HOME` path, no Git branch, HEAD or dirty state, no task or plan state, no session or run id, no model name, no token or size estimate, and no result of environment detection. No whole-build digest is placed **before** the large repeatable content either: a digest at the top would make every change to a late segment destroy the match of the entire prefix, which is the exact opposite of the feature. Digests, counts and every other changing diagnostic live in the sidecar; the section boundaries inside the text stay fixed (`#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`). PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-CARRY-NO-TOKEN-BUDGET` already settles that a generated boot artifact carries no size budget, and the same reasoning applies here: the prefix's size is the sum of what the resolution says the session must have, and padding it to reach a provider's minimum cacheable length is explicitly forbidden (`#SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS`).

p.SYS-DETERMINISM: **Determinism is a property with named mechanics.** The segment order is fixed by `#SYS-BAND-ORDER`; the framing, encoding (UTF-8, no BOM) and line endings are fixed by `#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`; the continuation plan's order is the existing INDEX order and no other traversal; and nothing is summarised, re-wrapped, sorted by an unordered map, or stamped. The claim to be proved is therefore mechanical and testable: two checkouts of the same commit in different directories, on Linux, macOS and Windows, produce byte-identical `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json`, and a repeated generation with unchanged inputs rewrites neither file (`#SYS-NO-EQUAL-REWRITE`), so it does not even move an mtime.

p.SYS-INVALIDATION: **The invalidation table — what each kind of change does.** It is the user-facing summary of `#SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME` and the one thing a reader needs to predict the feature's behaviour.

identity.fence: change effect on the prefix / the request -------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------- new question, time, current plan, cwd nothing; only band T changes. The prefix is never built from any of these values. bytes of an applicable dynamic boot file, prefix unchanged and still valid; a fresh band U/G plan unchanged suffix is read per request. Existing installed- integrity rules continue to apply. template, entrypoint, static-lane input, prefix stale. `check` says so and names why; recipe or lane_form regeneration is explicit. Stale bytes are never sent as current. INDEX composition or order, a condition, the pairing is invalid: recompute the boot plan and visibility, selected node, package binding republish the affected artifacts. Never mix two generations of prefix and sidecar. model, tools, SDK wrapper, request framing the file may be identical while the provider's actual cached prefix differs. A local digest is not a remote cache identity. provider TTL expiry a new cache write may be needed with a completely unchanged SYSTEM.md.

p.SYS-BASELINE-CORRECTIONS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — where the 2026-11-07 research was wrong about the code, recorded so the plan's baseline is not re-derived.** Verified against `e2508fc1d`. **(1)** `own_boot.rs` is **not** `crates/vibe-workspace/src/own_boot.rs`; it is `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/own_boot.rs` (226 lines), a private submodule declared at `install/bootgen.rs:346-347`. **(2)** `conditions.rs` is **not** under `boot_artifacts/`; it is `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/conditions.rs` (97 lines), used from `install/bootgen.rs:60`. **(3)** `legacy_entries` does **not** exclude "only" the three generated names: it also skips non-regular files (`:177-179`) and everything `vibe_specdoc::is_spec_source` rejects (`:181-183`), and it hard-errors on a Markdown/XML name collision (`:212-222`) — which matters, because `is_spec_source` accepts by extension alone, so both new `.md` paths are admitted today and `#SYS-SELF-INCLUSION`'s gate is required, not optional. **(4)** `generated_boot_paths` is private and returns boot-dir-relative **paths**, not bare names (`layout.rs:250-255`), so the reservation is an edit to that one private list plus two new public accessors, not a new predicate per caller. **(5)** The research's own refusal to trust a source comment was right: the unresolved-link fallback in `boot.rs:355-359` is `unwrap_or_default()` and `LinkType`'s `#[default]` sits on `Dynamic` (`crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package.rs:405`), while the comment at `boot.rs:352-354` says the final fallback is `static` and is wrong. **(6)** The boot transaction's role set is **closed and validated**, not open: `boot_artifacts/transaction/journal.rs:62-86` admits exactly `INDEX.md`, `STATIC.md` and `STATIC.xml` as production targets, requires the selected/stale pair to be exactly that distinct `STATIC` pair (`:75-78`), and `transaction.rs:259-282` requires all targets to share one parent directory and be distinct — so `#SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES` is a real change to that owner and nothing about a new filename is transactionally covered by default. The durable record is not called `Transaction`: `journal.rs:7-10` aliases the wire type `BootArtifactTransaction` as `Journal`, and the write input is `ArtifactWrite` (`transaction.rs:61-67`), holding the INDEX bytes, the optional selected STATIC bytes and the stale spelling to remove. **(7)** There is **not** one semantic lane compiler call but **three** independent prepare-and-compile sites, as `#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM` now records; a change to lane preparation must move all three, and a design that assumed one seam would silently miss the owner-managed and custom-backend lanes. Spike S4 refined what that costs the prefix: only the builtin and owner-managed seams publish a node's STATIC lane and they are selected once per regeneration rather than per node, while the custom-backend seam compiles `artifacts/<backend>` through an analyser query and is on no publication path — so the prefix's publication hooks are two, not three. **(8)** Four more research paths are wrong, all under `crates/vibe-workspace/src/`: `publish_node_boot` is `install/bootgen/publication.rs:13`, not `boot_artifacts/publication.rs`; the unit fingerprint is `boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs`, not `install/bootgen/fingerprint.rs`, which does not exist; owner-plan digest frames are `install/bootgen/owner_plans.rs:15`, not `boot_artifacts/owner_plans.rs`; static-zone membership and order are `boot/hybrid.rs` with hoisting in `boot/hybrid/hoist.rs`, not `boot_artifacts/hybrid.rs`; and the node-dependency projection is `install/bootgen/node_dependency.rs:14`. **(9)** The research's "StaticTransitive forces descendants **except residual OS gates**" is **wrong at HEAD**: `boot/hybrid.rs:244-288` `descend` never consults a contribution's `when`, and says so in code at `:263-265` — a gated target joins the static zone like any other, and gates act later, in `has_static_boot` / `static_boot_count` (`:135-151`) and in the fragment filter of `install/bootgen/node_dependency.rs:108-111`. Four doc comments still claim the old behaviour (`boot/hybrid.rs:17-20`, `:118-121`, `boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs:10-11`, `boot/hybrid/hoist.rs:16`); they are stale and must not be cited as behaviour. This matters here only as a warning about the source of truth, since `#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX` keeps every gate in band G regardless. **(10)** `vibe check` does **not** validate the spec-XML dialect, and no `cargo xtask` subcommand or test walks `vibevm/vibespecs/**` to parse it; the only authoritative validator is the PROP-045 projector `vibe_specdoc::project_spec_text` (`crates/vibe-specdoc/src/load.rs:140`), reached corpus-wide through `vibe facts check` or per file through `vibe refactor convert-source --dry-run`, which parses but always exits 0. Adding a dialect check is a candidate recorded in the app-versions campaign log, not a thing this campaign may assume exists.

p.SYS-CAPTURE-REUSE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — capture reuses the existing retained observations and adds no new reader.** The prefix's inputs are admitted through the owners that already hold them under a held workspace: the prepared node boot carrier with its observed policy, media and bytes (`install/bootgen/own_boot.rs`, whose `PreparedNodeBoot` holds `entries`, `root`, `relative`, `policy` and `captured`, and whose `recheck()` re-validates them), the declared-source bindings and generated observations (`boot_artifacts/declared_sources.rs`), the generated-input admission that captures before and after verification and refuses stale unit freshness (`install/bootgen/generated_inputs.rs`), and the read-only in-memory lane analysis (`install/bootgen/analyze.rs`). Three things capture does **not** do: it does not expand a home directory, a stewardship file, a plan, a custody record or a token path because some authored sentence mentions one (`#SYS-NO-HOME-EXPANSION`); it does not recursively follow prose links, `spec://` references or `#use` markers; and it does not read the whole host inventory — the scope is the selected node's boot scope, exactly as PROP-072 `#SOURCE-HOST-BOOT-LAW` bounds it. Classification is kept separate per lane: an INDEX row is classified as a continuation row, not as a static-link contribution, and the two are never merged into one list.

p.SYS-PROSPECTIVE-ENTRYPOINT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the entrypoint witness is the prospective one of the same generation, never the file as it was before the write.** The same publication can rewrite the entrypoint's managed block: `boot_artifacts.rs:365` `write_boot_artifacts_inner` compiles the INDEX body and the static artifact first (`:379-391`), then calls `transaction::write_production_with_selectors` (`:405`) whose selector closure (`:413-415`) runs `redirect::write_redirect_blocks_with_transaction` **after** the INDEX/STATIC roll-forward commits (`transaction.rs:245`), and the replacement content itself depends on the target spec format. Witnessing the pre-write entrypoint would make a newly published prefix stale the instant it was written, or bind it to the wrong generation. So the prospective managed-redirect projection is computed through that same redirect owner, the source-before and expected-source-after are retained separately, and the prefix, the sidecar and any changed redirect are published and checked as **one coherent generation**. The entrypoint is never re-read after publication to manufacture agreeing evidence.

p.SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES: **Decided 2026-11-10 — two new production roles inside the existing boot transaction, and no second atomicity story.** `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json` become two new `StageRole`s and two new admitted production targets in `boot_artifacts/transaction/journal.rs` (whose target list `:21-23` and validation `:62-86` are closed today), staged in `transaction/prepare.rs` and applied beside the INDEX and STATIC roll-forwards in `transaction.rs`. They are *inside* the existing commit, not a parallel writer: a failure must never leave a new prefix paired with a sidecar of another generation, nor damage the previous usable set. The whole output set is computed and validated **before** publication, the relevant captured inputs are rechecked immediately before the write (as `boot_artifacts.rs:402-404` already does), and the selected-source-member protection of PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-PAIR` is preserved unchanged: `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/publication.rs:13` `publish_node_boot` refuses to publish into a nonroot authored package member selected as a dependency by `(kind, group, name)` with version absent from the predicate (`:24-28`), and the two new roles are inside that same refusal rather than beside it. The `common_parent` invariant (`transaction.rs:259-282`) holds trivially, since all five targets live in the one boot directory. There is no second journal.

p.SYS-NO-EQUAL-REWRITE: **Equal bytes are not rewritten.** Publication already skips a write whose content equals what is on disk (`boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:267-269` and `transaction/selector.rs:21-23`), and the two new roles use the same rule, so an idempotent regeneration produces no write, no mtime change and no git diff — which is also the mechanical form of the first acceptance condition. A regeneration must never grow the file: the same inputs give the same length, and a prefix that grows on a second run is a self-inclusion bug by definition.

p.SYS-REMOVAL-AND-CONFLICT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — opting out, and the file that is not ours.** Removing `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` makes the node opt out, and the next install removes exactly the two outputs it can prove it owns — proof being the sidecar's own witness of the pair, by the same reasoning the publication already uses to delete the *stale* STATIC spelling while never touching the selected one (`boot_artifacts.rs:401`, `transaction/prepare.rs:90`). A `SYSTEM.md` present with **no** sidecar, with a sidecar that does not describe it, or whose bytes do not match the sidecar's `prefix_sha256`, is an **ownership conflict**: a named refusal that writes nothing and deletes nothing, because a file by that name may be a user's own work. A hand-edited output is never silently blessed as current and never silently overwritten; the user is told which file, which mismatch, and the exact command that would regenerate it deliberately. Switching lane spelling, changing the entrypoint or changing the recipe is an ordinary regeneration of a coherent set, not a removal.

p.SYS-OPERATIONS-SURFACE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — generation on install, and one new top-level command namespace with three verbs.** Generation happens inside the install, reinstall, format-change and staged-publication paths that already publish boot artifacts, for every node that has opted in; nothing is generated at session boot, and boot stays pure file reading. The explicit surface is `vibe prompt`, a free top-level name today: **`vibe prompt build`** writes the outputs through `#SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES`; **`vibe prompt check [--json]`** compares the current inputs with the published artifacts and reports `equal` / `stale` / `missing` / `conflict` / `unavailable` / `freshness_unverifiable` with the reasons; **`vibe prompt prepare --json`** returns the materials of `#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE` — bands P, U and G separately, with their observed digests, the recommended cache boundaries and the unresolved remainder. `prepare` returns **materials and observations, never a ready-to-send request**: it does not assemble credentials, choose a model or construct a provider envelope, and its grammar is settled together with its first real consumer rather than shipped as flags that parse and are ignored.

p.SYS-OPERATIONS-PATH-AND-FLAGS: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — a caller must be able to ask where the artifacts are, and every build must say what it did.** **`vibe prompt path [--part lane|system] [--json]`** prints the absolute path of a generated artifact. There are two parts because there are two artifacts: `lane` is `AGENT-LANE.md` (`#SYS-AGENT-LANE`), what a launch or import delivery points at, and `system` is the API prefix `SYSTEM.md`. `--json` adds size, hash and freshness. **A stale or missing artifact is reported as stale or missing, with the exact `vibe prompt build` that fixes it — never as an empty path**, because an empty path is the one answer a shell alias silently turns into a broken launch. **`vibe prompt flags --harness <name>`** prints ready-to-paste launch flags for that harness, aligned with `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` §8.4 (for Claude Code: `--append-system-prompt-file <lane>` together with `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`). **Whoever builds the artifacts ends with one summary line naming what happened and where** — `vibe install` when the project has opted in, and `vibe prompt build`: `system prompt: rebuilt → <abs SYSTEM path> (<size>), lane → <abs LANE path> (<size>)`, or `system prompt: unchanged → <path>`. A failed build and an opted-out project each say so explicitly rather than staying silent, and the same facts appear in the command's `--json` report. Both surfaces are tested offline.

p.SYS-READ-ONLY-CHECK: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `check` and `prepare` are effect-free, and the boundary is a capability contract rather than a sandbox promise.** Neither writes a product, cache, profile or config file; neither opens a network connection; and — the part that is easy to get wrong — neither invokes an effectful native or backend compile provider to recompute freshness. Reusing an analyse entrypoint is not by itself proof of that, and the distinction is per function rather than per module: `analyze_node_lane` (`install/bootgen/analyze.rs:80`) takes no provider and is effect-free, while `analyze_node_lane_bound_native_using` (`:270`), `analyze_effective_bound_native_with_sources` (`:554`) and `compile_node_backend_using` (`:415`) each accept an `OwnerNativeCompileProvider` — the last one mandatorily — and hand control to a caller-supplied trait whose invocation may spawn a process or reach the network (`boot_artifacts/native_managed/explicit.rs:71-73`, `native_managed.rs:332`), with native continuations bound to owner runtime epochs. So "we called analyse" establishes nothing; naming the exact function does. What `check`/`prepare` may do is read retained inputs, compare witnesses, and run only explicitly effect-free builtin preparation. When the needed proof is impossible without an effectful provider — a pending native unit, a stale generated substitution, an unadmittable generated input — the answer is `freshness_unverifiable` or `unavailable` **with** the explicit `vibe prompt build` that would resolve it. **Measured 2026-11-10 by spike S5, and it sets a real budget.** Provider-free `analyze_node_lane` does succeed on the host node with no provider, returning the 251,817-byte artifact byte-equal to the committed lane over 26 attributed inputs with none unattributable — but it takes **328–342 ms warm** on three consecutive runs, after a 1.1 ms `Workspace::load`. That is far too slow to sit in an API caller's request path unconditionally, so `prepare` and `check` answer from the sidecar's own witnesses first and escalate to analysis only on a mismatch; the escalation is the exception, not the path. S5 also produced the first concrete `unavailable` member for the list above, for free and before any compile: an incomplete checkout whose selected slot cannot be admitted refuses in 1.7 ms (`selected slot no-follow admission refused`), which is a world-integrity refusal rather than a freshness one and must be reported as `unavailable` with its path, never silently treated as "no lane". It never falls back to an empty transform plan, never quietly repairs while promising no writes, and never becomes an implicit install. `prepare` is the calling program's preflight, run outside the model's turn; the transport contract never asks an agent to run it (`#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT`).

p.SYS-SESSION-TARGET: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a gated row is evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target, never against the generator's host.** The condition grammar is closed and already exact: `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package/when.rs:71-112` accepts `os:windows` / `os:macos` / `os:linux` and `installed:<group>/<name>` and refuses anything else by name, and the enum has exactly those two variants. `installed:` is a **generation-time** decision owned by `install/bootgen/conditions.rs:86-96` — false drops the contribution entirely, true removes the condition — so only an `os:` gate survives into band G. `prepare` therefore requires an explicit session target when band G is non-empty; an absent or unknown target is **unresolved input**, reported as such, and never resolved to the operating system of whatever machine once generated the prefix. An unknown selector never becomes `true`. The prefix itself stays portable **when the node says so**, which is the default; the owner's decision of 2026-11-10 makes baking an OS an explicit per-project choice rather than the rejected alternative it was when this fact was written — see `#SYS-HOST-AND-TARGET`, which supersedes `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q3 and governs this fact wherever the two differ. Everything above still describes the `host = "portable"` case exactly.

p.SYS-HOST-AND-TARGET: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — two platform axes, not one, and they are different questions. This supersedes `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q3's "portable, full stop" default.** The manifest's `[system_prompt]` gains two optional keys: `host = "portable" | "linux" | "windows" | "macos"` (default `"portable"`) and `target = ["linux", …]` (default: every operating system). **`host` is where the agent runs; `target` is what the product is for**, and the case that proves they cannot be one key is ordinary: a Linux workstation building Windows software. **`host` governs the existing `when = "os:<name>"` gate**, which has always meant the session's own operating system — a devops, shell or package-manager rule. `"portable"` keeps the behaviour this document already specifies: an `os:` row stays in the gated continuation band and is evaluated per session against an explicitly supplied session target (`#SYS-SESSION-TARGET`). A **fixed** OS resolves those rows at build time and bakes them into the prefix — a matching row is included, a non-matching row is dropped — so a fixed-host prefix has an empty band G and `prepare` needs no session target for it. When a session's own OS then differs from the fixed host, `vibe prompt check` and `vibe prompt prepare` **warn and continue; they do not refuse**: the prefix is a deliberate project declaration, and refusing would make a cross-platform worker unable to read its own project's instructions. **`target` introduces a new gate spelling, `when = "target:<os>"`**, for a rule about the platform the software itself addresses — a kernel interface, WinAPI, a filesystem semantic. Because that is a property of the project and never of a session, it is **always** resolved at build time, whatever `host` says: a `target:` row is included exactly when its OS is in `target`, and an absent `target` selects every OS, so **no existing project's boot changes**. A `target:` row therefore never reaches band G, and the band model of `#SYS-BANDS` is unchanged — only `os:` rows can be gated, and only under `host = "portable"`. **Two consequences worth stating before someone reads them as contradictions.** First, a baked host OS is **not** a violation of `#SYS-NO-VOLATILE`'s ban on "the result of environment detection": nothing is detected. The OS name is read from the node's own authored manifest, exactly like `entrypoint` or `recipe`, so the prefix stays a pure function of its declared inputs and `#SYS-DETERMINISM` holds unchanged — two checkouts of one commit still produce identical bytes, on every host. Detecting the generating machine's OS remains forbidden. Second, two projects that declare different hosts get different prefixes, which is correct: they have different inputs. **Where the work lands.** The `[system_prompt]` keys, their closed value sets and their refusals are **implemented in P1**: an unknown OS refuses naming the field, every legal OS and `portable`; `target = []` refuses, because an empty selection and an absent key mean opposite things and `[]` would silently drop every `target:` row; a repeated OS refuses. The `when = "target:<os>"` grammar itself — a third variant in the closed condition set of `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package/when.rs:71-112`, resolved at generation time beside `installed:` in `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/conditions.rs:86-96`, and therefore never a residual `when` in `INDEX.md` — lands in **P2**, where the continuation plan is classified and `conditions.rs` is already being read. Baking `os:` rows under a fixed host lands in **P3** with the composer, and the host-mismatch warning in **P5** with `check` and `prepare`. The format record is `SP-FMT-101`.

api.title: 8. The API boundary, authority and agent modes

p.SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a filename chooses no API role, and moving repository text into an instruction role is not semantically neutral.** A supported adapter places the project's trusted instructions explicitly in a supported instruction role (`system`, `developer`, or the equivalent provider field), preserving any mandatory external instructions and the user-set boundaries that already apply. The elevation is acknowledged rather than assumed away: project instructions, package boot text, examples and operational grants do not acquire provider-level authority merely by being on disk or by being in a file called `SYSTEM.md`, and a text separator inside one message creates no real role boundary. The one thing a repository file cannot do is fix an agent that does not let its caller control its own prefix or its auto-loading; such an agent is simply not part of the guaranteed integration, and saying so is more useful than pretending a Markdown file solves it.

p.SYS-NO-DOUBLE-INJECTION: **A supported adapter never injects the prefix and then auto-loads the same entrypoint or lane again.** Supplied sources are accounted for explicitly, which is the only reason the transport contract can say what it says. Double injection is the failure this feature most plausibly produces — it would double the cost it exists to reduce while leaving the agent two copies of the same instructions — so it is a named qualification scenario proved by capturing the actual request against a local fake provider, not an assurance.

p.SYS-WORKER-EXCLUSION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a quiet worker does not receive the central prefix at all, not even briefly.** The profile and the packet are selected **before** the request is constructed, so the central prefix is never assembled for a bounded worker; there is no "ignore the parts that do not apply to you" clause in the prefix and there is deliberately no attempt to write one. A later message cannot return spent context and cannot restore a delegation boundary that has already been crossed. A central session gets the profile of its own selected node; a root's legitimate aggregation of its own subtree stays legitimate (PROP-009 `#MATRYOSHKA-SCOPES`), and the rule is "no content from outside the selected effective scope", not "no members".

p.SYS-NO-HOME-EXPANSION: **Nothing user-local is pulled in by reference.** An authored instruction that *mentions* a home directory, a stewardship settings or plan file, a custody or handoff record, or a token path is an instruction to a tool-using agent, not permission to embed that file's contents; the exporter opens none of them. Package boot text and ordinary repository documents do not acquire instruction authority just because they sit on disk and are reachable. Legitimate user-local observations reach a session through an explicit runtime contract in band T, chosen per request by the caller — which is also what keeps an ostensibly shared prefix from differing by user and from accidentally publishing confidential material. The qualification for this is a sentinel test: the files exist, and they are proved never opened and never present in the output.

p.SYS-CACHE-FACTS: **Checked provider properties, 2026-11-07, recorded as evidence and not as a product contract.** OpenAI: the cache depends on matching the actual rendered prefix, including tools and other request parts; a stable instruction block helps, while retention, eligibility and write conditions depend on the model, and the hit must be read from real usage. Anthropic: the Messages API takes `cache_control` and the hierarchy is tools, then system, then messages, so a change to an early block affects later matches, and entries have a limited lifetime. Gemini: implicit caching exists and a common early prefix is recommended, while explicit caching depends on the API and model and is not universal. Specific prices, TTLs and model lists are deliberately **not** frozen into this document: they change, and a design that encoded them would be wrong within a quarter. A text artifact is not a portable KV cache, does not transfer between models or providers, does not by itself reduce the amount of context a session needs, and does not reconcile contradictory instructions. Stabilising a large prefix is not the same as deserving one: whether the boot a session loads should be that large at all remains a separate engineering question this feature does not answer.

p.SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS: **The economics are parametric, and a saving is claimed only when measured.** For a prefix of L tokens with W cache writes and H cache reads, compare `L × (W + H) × uncached_rate` against `L × (W × write_rate + H × read_rate) + storage_cost` where storage is billed, then add the uncacheable requests and the unchanged cost of the dynamic and output tokens. The numbers come from the current rates and the observed usage, never from this document. A first request and frequent expiries can reduce or erase the benefit entirely. Byte repeatability and the exact request envelope are provable offline against a fake provider; a claim about real money requires a separate measurement of cache write and read tokens, latency and cost on named models, which is **not** performed by this design and is authorised separately (`#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q5). Padding a prefix with useless text to reach a provider's minimum cacheable length is forbidden outright.

p.SYS-HARNESS-DELIVERY: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 — three delivery tiers, one mode per harness, and every launch mechanism is file-based. Adopted as decided from `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` (decisions D1–D12 of its §11), which is the design authority for the detail.** The tiers are **launch** (vibe hands the composed agent lane to the harness's own system/developer slot through `vibe agent <harness>`, before the first request), **import** (an `@path` line inside the managed block, which the harness inlines), and **read** (the router block of `#SYS-NO-RECURSION` tells the agent to read the files with its tools). The setting is `[system_prompt.harness.<name>] delivery`, default `launch` for `claude` and `codex` and `read` for every other harness; it decides both the managed block's shape and what `vibe agent` does. **`import` is reserved and refused in version 1**, with a message naming its four blockers: it cannot be chosen per harness while the three entrypoint files are byte-identical (so one import line reaches every import-processing harness and would deliver the lane twice), the lane is not import-inert (`#SYS-IMPORT-INERTNESS`), it is unconditional and so reaches quiet workers in violation of `#SYS-WORKER-EXCLUSION`, and it follows a harness's downward discovery into nested projects. **Ambient config carriers are refused outright** — a project file a harness reads on every launch (`.codex/config.toml`, OpenCode `instructions`, pi `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`) lands in the slot like launch but is unconditional like import, so it too reaches quiet workers. For Codex the carrier is instead a launch-time profile file, and `vibe agent codex` **may** write `$CODEX_HOME/vibe-<node-id>.config.toml` — written only by `vibe agent` and `vibe prompt flags`, never by an install — because the alternative is no launch tier for Codex at all. **No lane bytes ever go on a command line.** A single argument is capped at 128 KiB on Linux (measured: 200,000 bytes refused, 120,000 accepted) and the whole command line at about 32,767 characters on Windows, while the lane is about 310 KB — so the inline route fails on every operating system, not only Windows, and a harness with no file-based slot simply has no launch tier. Three further decisions, each stated so it is not re-argued: the slot carries the **lane only**, not the template, which is written for an API runner with no base prompt and can contradict a harness's own; `vibe agent claude` passes `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`; and `vibe agent` performs **no** OS detection to bake `os:` rows under `host = "portable"`, leaving them to the router, which keeps the artifact a pure function of declared inputs. An entrypoint whose managed block would fall outside Codex's 32 KiB `project_doc_max_bytes` truncation is a **refusal**, and a warning within 4 KB of it. The safe-by-construction property that makes `launch` a defensible default before any live run: a project in `launch` mode started *plain* simply has no markers in context, and the router reads — so the two tiers share one byte-identical block and a project can never contradict itself. Format record: `SP-FMT-105`.

p.SYS-NO-RECURSION: **Owner requirement 2026-11-10 — no recursion and no inconsistency across harnesses, including the ones that put the instruction file into the system prompt. This supersedes the earlier sketch in which agent mode imported `SYSTEM.md`.** **Agent mode never delivers `SYSTEM.md`.** `SYSTEM.md` contains the entrypoint, and a harness has already loaded the entrypoint, so importing the prefix *from* the entrypoint is entrypoint → prefix → entrypoint recursion and double delivery with two contradicting managed blocks. Agent mode delivers the **lane** (`#SYS-AGENT-LANE`); `SYSTEM.md` stays the API artifact. **Composition proves the other direction closed:** the prefix's entrypoint segment replaces the managed block with fixed text that contains **no `@` import line and no router**, and the composer *verifies* the composed bytes contain neither — so even a mistaken import of `SYSTEM.md` cannot recurse. **The router scopes itself.** It governs only the project whose root holds the file it sits in; a managed block a harness concatenated in from a sub-directory or a dependency copy is not this session's boot and is ignored, and a task carrying the subagent quiet clause ignores the block entirely. `vibe` **neutralises** the managed block in the copies it materialises under `vibedeps/`, and `vibe check` warns about a nested managed block reachable by a harness's downward discovery. **Several instruction files are mutually consistent by construction.** Gemini CLI and Qwen Code (a Gemini CLI fork) both process `@path` imports recursively, both discover context files in parent *and* sub-directories and concatenate them, and both can be configured to read several names (`AGENTS.md` plus `QWEN.md`). So the router's test is "the lane is present **anywhere** in your context", never "above": concatenation order, and which of two files carries the router, cannot change the outcome. Duplicated bytes are a stated cost, never a contradiction. Verified repository facts behind this: 19 tracked instruction files carry a `<vibevm>` managed block, and tracked `GEMINI.md` files exist under `research/rust-demo`, `research/ts-demo`, `vibevm/vibedeps/org.vibevm.fractality.delegation-rules/1.0.0` and `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.fractality/{delegation-rules,fractality}/v1.0.0`. Design document: `HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` §3 and §4.

p.SYS-IMPORT-INERTNESS: **Owner requirement 2026-11-10 — imported content must be inert for the harness that imports it, and today the lane is not.** `STATIC.xml` carries 68 tokens of the form `@spec://…`, and five of the eight INDEX files carry `@` tokens too. Gemini CLI and Qwen Code process `@path` recursively inside imported content, and Claude Code does so to a depth limit, so an imported lane could make a harness try to resolve a `spec://` address as a file path. `vibe` composes the lane **verbatim** (`#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`) and therefore may not rewrite those tokens. Two consequences. `import` stays refused until either boot text stops emitting such tokens or a live run shows a given harness leaves them alone — and the test is **per harness and per flavour**: before choosing an import flavour `vibe` verifies there is no triggering token outside a code fence, and otherwise falls back to router-only delivery, where the file is read through the agent's file tool and no import processing happens at all. `vibe prompt check` reports the token count and the first few locations.

p.SYS-BOOT-ORDER-IS-PRECEDENCE: **Owner decision 2026-11-10 (D12) — the boot order is an order of precedence, not of position, and PROP-009 gains one sentence saying so.** PROP-009 `#SESSION-START-ORDER` reads as a sequence in time: the entrypoint, then `STATIC`, then the INDEX entries. In launch delivery the lane arrives **first**, and in a stronger role. Rather than leave the published contract quietly false, the rule is restated: a conforming delivery may place the lane before the entrypoint, and a lane delivered earlier counts as read. Two honest consequences. Lane text gains instruction-role authority it does not have as a tool result, which `#SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT` already requires be acknowledged rather than assumed away. And authored text that refers to *position* — "above", "below", "you have just read" — breaks silently; `vibe prompt check` lists such phrases in the entrypoint and the lane for a human to review, and never edits them (`#SYS-NO-REWRITE-OF-AUTHORED-TEXT`).

p.SYS-HARNESS-EXECUTABLE: **Owner decision 2026-11-10, revised the same day — a launcher is a named thing with a kind, and only a user may name one. This amends `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/HARNESS-DELIVERY.md` §8.4, which named the programs directly.** The harness *kind* and the program that runs are two different things, and conflating them was the mistake. A **kind** — `claude`, `codex`, …, a closed set — is the flag dialect and the delivery rules: which slot, which flags, which refusals. A **launcher** is a name bound to a kind and to the argv that starts it. The motivating case is ordinary: a developer reaches a harness through a small personal wrapper that sets the harness's own config directory, drops API-key environment variables and `exec`s the real program with standing flags, passing every argument through. **The shape, in the user configuration only.** `[agent.launchers.<name>]` with `kind` (required, the closed set), `command` (the argv **prefix** to exec — a prefix rather than a path, so a wrapper may carry its own arguments) and an optional `config_dir`. `vibe agent <launcher-name> [args…]` resolves the launcher **by name**, takes its flags and delivery from its kind, and execs `command` + flags + the user's own arguments. The built-in launchers `claude` and `codex` always exist, each with `kind` equal to its name and `command` the program of that name; a user launcher of the same name **overrides** the built-in, which is how a wrapper takes over the plain name without the user retyping it. Any number of launchers may share a kind — two Claude Code launchers with different `config_dir`s are an ordinary configuration, not an edge case — and `vibe agent list` prints each one's name, kind, command, config directory and **source**, built-in or the exact user-config path, because a developer debugging which program ran needs to know which file decided it. An unknown launcher name is a refusal that **lists the available launchers**; an unknown kind is a refusal naming the field. `vibe prompt flags` accepts either a kind or a launcher name. **A project manifest that names a launcher is a refusal.** A repository must not choose which program runs on a contributor's machine: that is the one setting where a shared file would let one developer's convenience execute arbitrary code on everyone else's computer, and it is not a judgement call. **`config_dir` exists for one honest reason:** it names where that launcher's harness keeps its session logs, which the cache diagnostics of `#SYS-CACHE-FACTS` read. A wrapper that sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` internally makes the directory unknowable from outside — vibe sees neither the variable nor the harness's default — so a launcher may state it; absent that, vibe takes it from the environment, and absent that, the kind's documented default. **When it is still unknown the diagnostics say so**, rather than guessing a path and reading someone else's logs. Finally, `vibe prompt flags` prints **flags only and never a program**, which is what lets its output be appended to any wrapper, alias or launcher a developer already has. Offline tests: resolution by name; a user launcher overriding a built-in; an argv-prefix exec proved against a shim on `PATH` that records the argv it received; the unknown-name and unknown-kind refusals; the refusal of the table in a project manifest; and `vibe agent list`'s output. *(The first form of this decision, superseded within the day and never implemented, put the override on the kind itself as `[agent.<harness>] command` with a `--command` flag and a `VIBE_AGENT_<HARNESS>_COMMAND` variable above it. It could not express two launchers of one kind, which is the case that matters, and a per-run flag plus an environment variable is three precedence tiers where a name needs none.)*

layering.title: 9. Forward compatibility with the user and override layers
