p.SYS-LAYER-ROLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — this document specifies the `project` layer of PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX`, and says so in the artifact.** That fact composes one cache-stable prefix from the project layer, the global user project and the project override, in the precedence order of PROP-074 `#OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE`, with the project layer **first** precisely because it is the most shared and most stable, so that the project's own prefix stays a byte-identical leading part of the composed one. The sidecar therefore carries `layer = "project"` from version 1 and every segment id is layer-qualified from version 1, even though no other layer exists yet. Without a user project or override the composed prefix **is** the project prefix, so the artifact this document specifies is already the whole answer for a project that composes nothing.

p.SYS-LAYER-CONCATENATION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the four properties that let a later campaign compose layers with no format change here.** **(1) No document-level frame.** The prefix has no opening or closing wrapper, no table of contents and no "this document has N parts" preamble; every separator between *layers* belongs to the composer, and the project layer's bytes end with exactly one LF so a following layer concatenates cleanly (`#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`). **(2) No total digest in the text.** `prefix_sha256` is the project layer's own digest and lives in the sidecar; the composite's digest is the composer's own artifact and never appears inside any layer, so adding a layer cannot change a byte of the project layer. **(3) Layer-qualified ids.** Segment ids and input roles are namespaced by layer, so two layers' sidecars merge without collision and a composer can address one segment of one layer. **(4) A layer-scoped transport contract.** The contract of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT` speaks only for its own layer's supplied sources, so a composer appends each layer's contract instead of regenerating one global one. The composed prefix is personal and must never be committed, which is PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION`'s rule and that campaign's business — this document's artifacts are committed, and the two are different files in different places.

p.SYS-LAYER-NO-FORMAT-CHANGE: **The prediction this section makes, so it can be falsified.** When the layered-prefix campaign lands, it adds a composer and a personal uncommitted output; it must need **no** change to `vibe-system-prompt/1`, to the segment framing, to the transport-contract recipe or to the three reserved paths. If it does need one, this section was wrong, and the honest record of that is an amendment to this fact rather than a quiet format bump.

p.SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS: **Open to the owner, each with the default this design takes unless the owner says otherwise.** **(Q1) Is the unconditional INDEX band a cacheable continuation, or baked into the prefix?** Default: **cacheable continuation** (`#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE`) — the bytes are cached either way, and baking them would contradict `kind = "static"`'s actual meaning, make freshness much harder to prove, and buy nothing. The alternative, a target-bound fully-frozen snapshot, is a genuinely different contract with a freshness limit, and it would have to be offered as a second profile rather than as this one's default. **(Q2) What override authority do repository, package and user-preference instructions have once they sit in the API instruction role?** Default: the project layer is a trusted application scaffold carrying scoped project policy, user-local preference material never enters the prefix at all, and mandatory external instructions and user-set boundaries are preserved above it; the design does **not** assume the agent-side override semantics carry over unchanged, because the role is not the same role. **(Q3) Portable prefix with gated continuation, or target-bound prefix? ANSWERED by the owner 2026-11-10, and the answer is neither default alone: it is a per-project choice on two separate axes.** See `#SYS-HOST-AND-TARGET`, which governs. `host` (default `"portable"`) decides whether the session's-OS `os:` gates stay in band G or are baked in; `target` (default: every OS) is a new `target:` gate for the product's own platform and is always resolved at build time. The question was posed as one axis and it was two: the proposed default was right for the agent's host and had no answer at all for the product's platform. The original reasoning, kept because it is still why `portable` is the default: OS gates stay in band G and are evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target (`#SYS-SESSION-TARGET`), which is what the committed INDEX design already does; a target-bound prefix is cheaper to send and strictly less reusable, and nothing in this repository needs it today, since every INDEX row here is currently unconditional. **(Q4) How much of the entrypoint must be represented byte-for-byte, versus authored afresh in the template?** Default: **all of it, verbatim**, with the one in-place managed-block substitution of `#SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE` — because no generic prose filter can infer which paragraphs the owner wants dropped, and silently dropping instructions is the worst available failure. The honest cost is `#SYS-ENTRYPOINT-IS-AN-INPUT`: a frequently-edited entrypoint means a frequently-rebuilt prefix, and the remedy is repository hygiene, not an exporter heuristic. **(Q5) Must a measured provider saving exist before the campaign closes?** Default: **no** — the campaign ships the parametric model, the method and the offline envelope proof, and a live cache measurement on named models is a separately authorised follow-up that spends real money and is never run inside the campaign (`#SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS`). **(Q6) Are the two generated artifacts committed, like `STATIC`/`INDEX`? ANSWERED by the owner 2026-11-10, against this default: they are NOT tracked.** See `#SYS-ARTIFACTS-NOT-TRACKED`, which governs. The default argued that a fresh clone needs no build and that the alternative "would make the prefix unavailable to exactly the zero-dependency case the boot model exists for" — and that was the error: the zero-dependency case is a *session reading files*, which the boot lane serves and the prefix does not. Every consumer of a prefix is a program already invoking `vibe`.

p.SYS-ACCEPTANCE: **The twelve conditions the feature is accepted against**, carried forward from the owner's research proposal and made mechanical where it was prose. (1) The same inputs give a byte-identical `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json` in different checkout locations and on Linux, macOS and Windows; a repeated generation neither grows the file nor rewrites it. (2) Neither the template nor either output becomes an ordinary boot input, in legacy discovery or in declared mode; a direct or indirect self-include is refused before any write; a prose mention is not a self-include. (3) Differential scenarios confirm the prefix's static-first order, the continuation's original INDEX order, installed visibility, and gate behaviour for all three operating systems. (4) XML, Markdown, mixed and generated-stream lanes are handled by their existing owners; an authored literal directive or fenced example never becomes an executable import. (5) Root, member and specspace profiles receive nothing outside their selected effective scope while a root's permitted subtree aggregation is preserved, and a quiet worker never receives the central prefix, even temporarily. (6) A change of dynamic bytes under a compatible plan changes only the fresh suffix; a change of the template, the entrypoint or the lane makes the prefix detectably stale with no hidden rebuild. (7) A missing, unsupported or mutated input, an invalid marker and an output conflict each leave the previous coherent set intact. (8) Home, plan, custody and token sentinel files are never opened and never appear in the output without an explicit separate runtime input; the current task and time never change the prefix. (9) A fake provider sees the exact roles, block and tool order, prefix boundary and the absence of a duplicate entrypoint injection — and this does not count as a live cache hit. (10) `check` and `prepare` are proved read-only by filesystem, network and provider-call sentinels; no effectful callback runs even on a cache miss; install, reinstall and publish go through the one transaction owner. (11) The sidecar format and the invalidation reasons are versioned; an old consumer need not read the new artifact, and a project without the opt-in boots exactly as before. (12) A saving is claimed only after a separate provider measurement, and no useless text is ever added to reach a cache threshold.
